Preserve the foreground traveler, viewer-left distant walker, one calm pack mule with soft cloth cargo, exactly three upright foreground bark staffs, road, valley, treeless slopes, crop, palette, lighting and Wands rendering. Repaint only the entire viewer-right distant walker and its immediately adjacent narrow background footprint. Keep the same identity, ochre garment, dark hair, exact position, scale and walking-away direction, with one head, one torso and two separate walking legs and feet. Give this walker exactly two attached arms, two wrists and two object-free hands. Bend both arms naturally behind the body so one hand loosely holds the opposite wrist at the lower-back center. Keep the lower-back gesture inside the existing ochre torso-and-hip silhouette, with both upper arms connected at the shoulders. Garment straps, seams and belt ends also end inside the torso-and-hip silhouette. No continuous elongated mark may touch or emerge from either arm, hand or waist silhouette. Ordinary natural body contours, small disconnected road-and-rock texture and the cast shadow beneath the feet are allowed. Keep a visible background gap between the repainted walker and all mule tack. Do not move, enlarge, merge or rescale either walker, the mule or the three foreground staffs. Preserve exactly 3 people, 1 mule and 3 foreground staffs; add no fourth person, second animal, cart, wheel, rigid cargo frame, harness shaft, tree, branch, fence, post, mast, pole, rod, tool handle, fourth staff, text or other elongated object beyond the required three staffs. At full size require two anatomically continuous arms converging into one coherent behind-back wrist hold, with no missing, fused or duplicated limb and no outgoing elongated mark; do not require individually readable fingers. At 140×196 require only 3 people, 1 mule, 3 staff identities and no fourth rod-like line; do not enlarge hands for mobile readability.

It uses rejected attempt-004 as its sole source, preserves every other passing subject and scene invariant, and restores only the immediately adjacent background where the recurring line appeared.
